AI_EXPERT_DESCRIPTION:
Artificial Intelligence is not just a trend at my company. It is a core part of our development culture. We are required to actively integrate AI tools into our daily workflows, and I embrace this fully. Beyond the professional mandate, I invest my own time to deepen my understanding of AI, staying current with the rapid evolution of the field.
This commitment is backed by a Google certificate in AI, which I earned as a testament to my dedication. You can view it by clicking the image below. Whether it is leveraging AI-powered coding assistants, exploring large language models, or applying machine learning concepts to real-world problems, I am constantly learning and adapting to make the most of what modern AI has to offer.
At work we use Augment, an AI coding assistant very similar to Claude. In my own time, I am learning to use Claude, and the Anthropic certificates below confirm it. Because the two tools are so alike, I am effectively learning in two places at once: what I learn in one transfers directly to the other and makes me more effective in both.
ABOUT_ME_RICH_INTRO:
Greetings! My name is Amadeus, and I am a seasoned IT professional with a background in Software Development and an engineering degree. Since December 1, 2022, I have been employed as a developer, starting as an Angular Developer and growing into a full-stack role.
Currently, I specialize in Java EE and contribute to a large-scale core project that serves as the foundation for various customer implementations. My primary focus is on a solution developed for Swiss Life, though my journey began with contributions to AXA. These experiences have honed my skills in frontend and backend development, enabling me to tackle diverse challenges in web application development.
Thank you for visiting my personal page!
ABOUT_ME_RICH_DETAILS:
I have a deep passion for programming as it allows me to unleash my creativity and bring new ideas to life. Over the years, my expertise has grown to encompass both frontend and backend development, enabling me to work on large-scale core projects that have a real-world impact. My primary focus includes technologies like HTML, CSS, JavaScript, MongoDB, TypeScript, Tailwind, Angular, and Java EE, and I also have experience with frameworks like Bootstrap and Vue.
Beyond development, I’ve also worked as a network specialist in the IT industry, gaining valuable insights into system infrastructure. I also draw on skills from outside IT. Working as a sales assistant in a consumer electronics store significantly improved my communication and teamwork skills, and working in Dublin for Ryanair taught me attention to detail and how to work in an international environment. However, my true joy lies in coding, where I explore endless possibilities, collaborate with talented teams, and continually evolve my skills to tackle new challenges.

TMS-team-management-system.title: TMS - Team Management System
TMS-team-management-system.description: Made by a team of four people. Two of us were responsible for the front end and two for the back end. Unfortunately, my front-end teammate had COVID while we were building the beta version, which is now live. It's an MVP, but it works for clients who handle the management side of a team.

sneakers-shop.title: Sneakers Shop
sneakers-shop.description: A simple shop developed for small sellers focused on limited-edition sneakers. In the beta version, customers can log in and add items to the cart. Payments (e.g. via PayPal) and more features will be added in the future.

stockx-fix-extension.title: StockX Fix Extension
stockx-fix-extension.description: A small Tampermonkey extension that fixes StockX layout by automatically hiding sections of the website. It also allows adding items to a user's cart from external pages.

portfolio-site.title: Portfolio Site
portfolio-site.description: This is my personal portfolio showcasing all my previous work and projects. It's made with Angular and Tailwind CSS to create a responsive and lightweight website.

comarch-digital-insurance.title: Comarch Digital Insurance
comarch-digital-insurance.description: Comarch Digital Insurance (CDI) is a comprehensive digital platform designed for the insurance industry. It enables insurance companies to streamline their operations by automating processes such as policy creation, underwriting, claims management and customer service. CDI is highly customizable and can be integrated with external services like digital signatures, electronic identification and other tools to extend its functionality.

many-more.title: Many More Projects
many-more.description: Several other small projects, ranging from JavaScript and Python scripts to Angular apps and more. Check out my GitHub for the full list.

architecture.title: Architecture
architecture.description: The UI is built with Vue and Vuetify, which provide high responsiveness and readability on the user side. The server side of the application consists of several modules. An SQLite database handles data storage, and communication with the database is handled by the Django framework. We use Django REST Framework to send and receive data between the user interface and the application server.

dashboard.title: Coach Dashboard
dashboard.description: View showing the team's last 3 matches on the left, attendance at recent training sessions on the right, and a table at the bottom with detailed info about every player's score in the selected match. This view helps coaches quickly check the status of the last few days.

matches.title: Matches view
matches.description: Main view containing all matches. The user can add a match in 3 steps: event -> team games -> player scores. Error handling covers every user input mistake. If something fails, the user can add the missing pieces in the match detail view. The winning team is colored green. Adding and deleting training sessions works the same way as in the players and coaches views, to keep it simple for the user.

singleMatch.title: Single Match view
singleMatch.description: Detailed match view. Two tables with player scores, sortable by every parameter and editable by the user. The search field works with every parameter. If the user made an input mistake, this is where they can add the missing data. Every input has validation rules.

calendar.title: Calendar view
calendar.description: Calendar view for easily browsing upcoming events, including training sessions and matches. The user can also add a standalone event, for example 'team meeting'. The view can be switched between day, 4 days, week and month, with month as the default.

knowledgebase.title: Knowledgebase
knowledgebase.description: A place where users can find professional knowledge.

singleKnowledgebase.title: Single knowledgebase article
singleKnowledgebase.description: Single article view, with more details.

players.title: Players list
players.description: View with a table listing all players. Search works by first name, last name, gender and email. The table can be sorted by every parameter. Following the F-pattern, the edit and add buttons are in the top right corner.

playersAdd.title: Adding and editing Players
playersAdd.description: Adding players follows different rules depending on the player's team. If it's our player, the user has to fill in all the data. If not, only the first name, last name and gender are needed. The edit button adds an edit row to the table, allowing the user to delete/edit players.

trainings.title: Training sessions view
trainings.description: View containing all training sessions. The user can add and delete training sessions by clicking in the top right corner. Sorting by query was added in beta 0.2, so the live version will not match this screenshot. Clicking an individual training session opens its detail view.

trainingsAdd.title: Adding and editing training sessions
trainingsAdd.description: Adding and deleting training sessions works the same way as in the players and coaches views, to keep it simple for the user.

singleTraining.title: Single training session view
singleTraining.description: Here users can send notifications to players taking part in the selected training session and view more details about it.

mainPage.title: Main Page
mainPage.description: I have tried to keep it as simple as possible. Following the F/Z-pattern, the cart and login page are in the top right corner. The logo in the top left corner also links to the homepage. Product models can be sorted by main category and model.

productPage.title: Product Page
productPage.description: The product page is kept as simple as possible for the best readability.

login.title: Login
login.description: Users can log in and register using email and password.

loginFirebase.title: Login with Firebase
loginFirebase.description: Firebase manages and stores user credentials. The site has auto-login, so the state isn't lost on refresh, and auto-logout when the token expires.

cartNoItem.title: Cart (No Items)
cartNoItem.description: The empty cart page is designed to be user-friendly: it contains only a cart with 2 animated bubbles (pure CSS) and a button encouraging the user to go back to the main page and add something.

cartItem.title: Cart (Item Added)
cartItem.description: The cart page will show the total of the items, animations on delete and much more.

features.title: Features
features.description: Product models can be sorted by main category and model. I have also implemented displaying size availability information.

mainPageSm.title: Main Page (Mobile)
mainPageSm.description: On mobile, the navbar on the main page is moved from the top to the bottom to make it easier to use and more mobile-friendly.

mainPageSmSidebar.title: Mobile main page sidebar
mainPageSmSidebar.description: Sidebar buttons are moved to a menu on the left, opened with the hamburger icon.

more.title: More coming...
more.description: I am still working on this project. Items are currently stored only in local storage and there is no user data yet. The goal is to store items in Firebase, connect users to the database and add payments. The UI is not finished yet either and needs polishing.

allItemsWithout.title: All Items Without Filters
allItemsWithout.description: A list of all items with no filters applied.

allItems.title: Check all items button
allItems.description: Triggered by clicking the left button on the top navbar. Highlights items where the user's price is not actually the lowest.

itemWithout.title: Item view without extension
itemWithout.description: Image showing how StockX looks without the extension. After the user clicks check, the plugin adds two fields.

itemWith.title: Item view after using extension
itemWith.description: Fields added by the plugin calculate the real price the user should have entered to get the lowest ask and display it in the DOM. Another field calculates the user's payout, so they immediately know whether it's even worth placing an ask.

good.title: Well...
good.description: You are already on this site :D. Feel free to contact me with your feedback.

more.title: More coming
more.description: I am still working on this website. I want to add more animations to make it more user-friendly, work on mobile versions of images, make it more visible on Google and more...

cdi1.title: Health insurance support
cdi1.description: It simplifies the management of health insurance policies by offering tools for agents, brokers and back-office employees.

cdi2.title: Automated claims processing
cdi2.description: Integration with Comarch Insurance Claims allows for smooth claim handling.

cdi3.title: Compliance with regulations
cdi3.description: CDI adheres to industry standards like GDPR, IDD (Insurance Distribution Directive) and PRIIPs (Packaged Retail and Insurance-Based Investment Products).

cdi4.title: Cloud deployment
cdi4.description: The platform can be deployed in the cloud, offering scalability and accessibility.

cdi5.title: AI integration
cdi5.description: While AI is not built directly into CDI, Comarch offers a separate AI Framework that can be used for data-driven decisions and process automation.
